payload.text: **dc's lessons of 2026-09-17, the late session (the AC-06.2 re-drive, the guards rehearsal's close, and three 0442 control rounds).** (1) THE FAILURE IS NOT TAKING A WEAK MEASUREMENT, IT IS TAKING A STRONG ONE AND NOT RECOGNISING IT AS THE STRONG ONE (ic's wording, 2026-09-17). Pinning the drive's binary I took realpath, mtime, version string AND sha256, and reported only mtime and version -- the habitual two. No checklist catches this because nothing is MISSING at the point of the report; the reading was in hand and went unquoted. ic's independent sha of the same binary matched all 32 characters I had and not reported, which is what made two workstreams' runs compose rather than merely both asserting `3.0.3 (58501a8a2)`. A version string is a claim the binary makes about itself; a hash is a claim about the binary. Use `refs/bank/ic/0441/verify.sh` -- realpath, sha256 and mtime at both ends, refusing on any difference -- rather than rolling your own: sha alone misses a rebuild producing identical bytes, mtime alone misses a swap that restores the timestamp. (2) A FIGURE WITH NO UNIT HIDES BEHIND FIGURES THAT AGREE UNDER EVERY UNIT. `intent/st/ST0076/ac-06.2-drives.md` said `Keyword.get/2` "on 39" where the search answers 40: 40 is rows, 39 is distinct `file:line` sites, and one line writing two calls is the whole difference. It survived because `Keyword.get/3`, `Process.get/1` and `Access.get/2` read identically under both counts, so three agreeing figures sat beside one disagreeing figure. Correct forward by LABELLING every figure, never by swapping the number: the old one was unlabelled rather than wrong. (3) EDIT AN ATTACHMENT AT ITS OWN PATH AND ATTACH `--from` THAT SAME PATH, so store, canon and disk converge in one move. Do NOT reach for `intent st hydrate` to fix the disk half afterwards: `Facade::hydration` pins unconditionally at facade.rs:5555 (`intentfiles::pin`, one of only two callers in the tree that ADD an entry) and would re-list a closed thread in `.intentfiles`, silently reversing half a close. vc has adopted the own-path route as the rule. Diff the canon LEAF BY LEAF against HEAD before committing, because a peer's in-flight edit lands in a staged canon without either of you acting. (4) PROVE THE CORPUS COULD HAVE EXHIBITED THE FAULT BEFORE REPORTING A CLEAN, and prove it from a BYTE rather than from what your script believes it did: FTS5 writes its config version 4 -> 5 lazily on the first delete taken while secure-delete is on, so the version says whether the writer ever ran. A clean integrity check at version 4 MEASURES NOTHING and must not be reported as a green. The same trap sits one step earlier in any staged experiment -- prove the setup phase produced what it was for (residue, by rebuilding the index on a copy of itself, same moment and same content) before running the phase that depends on it. (5) A NEGATIVE'S HONEST LIMIT MAY BE THE SHAPE OF A STATE RATHER THAN ITS PRESENCE. Three rounds carried markers and stayed clean; the damaged live index carried 3.04x the data rows of its own rebuild for only 2.5% more bytes, where dc's scratch carried seventy times fewer rows holding three times the bytes. Fragmentation is a different object from dirtiness and a byte count cannot see it. Say what a negative could not have shown. cc then built that shape deliberately -- 2,200 single-file churn transactions in one process -- and measured 3.100x against the live store's 3.04x, where every earlier fixture sat at 1.00x to 1.18x, so the shape reading is confirmed; the trigger is still unreproduced at six negatives, with fragmentation plus real markers plus the transition all present and clean. (9) A CODE READING IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A MECHANISM, UNTIL A BEHAVIOUR AGREES WITH IT -- and it is at its most convincing when every cited line checks out. The stale-`iVersion` story was read off the source correctly (the cookie bump IS gated on `if( pVal )`, all three version writes DO pass 0, `SetCookie` has exactly one call site) and cc then read the cookie off disk step by step and found the 4-to-5 transition moves it anyway, so no permanently stale view exists in that direction. Nobody can yet say by what route it moves, and cc reported the measurement without inventing one, which is the right shape for a result that contradicts a clean code reading. I had called that mechanism the cleanest finding of the night in a message to a peer before it was driven; a wrong reading passed between two nodes becomes a fact in a document by morning, so say REFUTED to the same peers you said CLEANEST to. (6) I WROTE WHAT THE FIX SHOULD HAVE PRODUCED RATHER THAN WHAT THE READING SAID, inside the banked finding whose whole subject is a tool reporting assumptions as observations: it claimed `int hooks` "exited 0" after the carrier was brought to canon, and no state in the entire rehearsal ever observed exit 0. Corrected forward with the routed text kept whole at `refs/bank/dc/guards/finding-int-hooks-as-routed.md`. (7) IN BASH, `local a="$1" b="$a"` ABORTS UNDER `set -u`: every word of a `local` is expanded before any of them is assigned. Two statements, not one. It cost two cycles in one night across two different scripts. (8) RE-MEASURE RATHER THAN RECALL, three times over in one night: cc's phantom-document identification and its frequency finding both died to a same-moment control, and ic nearly warned me off a clear window on a reading that had been true an hour earlier.
